title: Which tiger pictures match the shape of image A?
description: The width to height of four tiger pictures are each reduced to the simplest form by dividing both terms by their highest common factor. The simplest forms are then compared with that of image A. Keeko's doubt is that two pictures match because both start with sixty.
teaching_notes: One idea: ratios are in proportion when their simplest forms are the same. Watch for students who match ratios by looking at only the first term.

source: Reduce the width to height ratios of images A (60 : 40), D (
video_script.why: The child needs a sure test for ratios that match, and the simplest form gives one that does not depend on the look of the picture.
video_script.substitution: Divide both terms by their highest common factor, then compare the simplest forms.
video_script.anchor: the book's tiger pictures: image A with the width to height of D, B and E
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says images A and E match because both start with sixty. The first terms agree but the simplest forms are three to two and one to one, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Only image D has the same simplest form as image eigh, three to two.

final_answer.spoken: image D, because sixty to forty and ninety to sixty are in proportion

hold_back: Answer: D is in proportion with A
maths_rules: image A: 60 : 40; HCF of 60 and 40 is 20; 60 ÷ 20 = 3 and 40 ÷ 20 = 2; simplest form 3 : 2
image D: 90 : 60; HCF is 30; 90 ÷ 30 = 3 and 60 ÷ 30 = 2; simplest form 3 : 2
image B: 40 : 20; HCF is 20; 40 ÷ 20 = 2 and 20 ÷ 20 = 1; simplest form 2 : 1
image E: 60 : 60; HCF is 60; 60 ÷ 60 = 1 and 60 ÷ 60 = 1; simplest form 1 : 1
only D matches 3 : 2, so 60 : 40 :: 90 : 60; the factor from A to D is 90 ÷ 60 = 3/2
Keeko's slip: A and E both start with 60, but 3 : 2 is not 1 : 1
video_script.design: One idea: the same simplest form means in proportion. Assumes the ratio and its terms. Wrong idea: matching first terms means matching ratios. The pictures stay for the whole video.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the tiger pictures.
<bookmark mark='a'/>The width to height of image eigh is sixty to forty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Image D is ninety to sixty, and image B is forty to twenty. Image E is sixty to sixty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these three match the shape of image eigh?

beats.on_screen: the four pictures hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='hcf'/>We divide both terms by their highest common factor.
<bookmark mark='simple'/>The ratio we get is called the simplest form.
<bookmark mark='prop'/>Two ratios with the same simplest form are called in proportion.

marks.given: the four ratios are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, image eigh is sixty to forty, and image D is ninety to sixty. Image B is forty to twenty, and image E is sixty to sixty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the simplest form of each ratio, and which are in proportion with A

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to reduce each ratio to its simplest form and compare with image eigh.

marks.a: the heading Image A is written
marks.hcf: HCF of 60 and 40 is 20 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, take image eigh.
<bookmark mark='hcf'/>The highest common factor of sixty and forty is twenty.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Sixty divided by twenty is three, and forty divided by twenty is two.
<bookmark mark='s'/>The simplest form is three to two.

marks.d: the heading Image D is written
marks.hcf: HCF of 90 and 60 is 30 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>Step two, take image D.
<bookmark mark='hcf'/>The highest common factor of ninety and sixty is thirty.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Ninety divided by thirty is three, and sixty divided by thirty is two.
<bookmark mark='s'/>The simplest form is also three to two.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Step three, take image B. Forty and twenty have the highest common factor twenty, which gives two to one.
<bookmark mark='e'/>For image E, sixty and sixty have the highest common factor sixty, which gives one to one.

marks.cmp: the four simplest forms are set side by side
marks.dd: A and D glow together with 3 : 2
marks.bb: B and E show in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step four, compare the four simplest forms.
<bookmark mark='dd'/>Only D matches three to two.
<bookmark mark='bb'/>Two to one and one to one are different.
<bookmark mark='f'/>The factor from image eigh to D is ninety divided by sixty, which is three halves.

beats.on_screen: Answer: D is in proportion with A, 60 : 40 :: 90 : 60; B and E are not
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Only image D has the same simplest form as image eigh, three to two.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears with A 60 : 40 and E 60 : 60
marks.first: the first terms 60 and 60 are circled in the bubble

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks images eigh and E match, because both start with sixty.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first terms are the same, but we must look at both terms.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Sixty to forty becomes three to two, and sixty to sixty becomes one to one.
<bookmark mark='simple'/>These simplest forms are different, so the ratios are not in proportion.
<bookmark mark='land'/>Image E is square, while image eigh is wider than it is high.
